tabs.title: Who they are
tabs.description: Gautham, 38, data science director — returned to the market two years after selling his first flat, discovered that every project he actually wants sold out at launches he didn't attend, and found the primary market's side door: buying an early investor's booking and inheriting a near-launch position in a sold-out tower.

buyers.name: Gautham Prabhu

chatMessages.text: Riya, update on the Nikoo assignment. The seller's fine with price, fine with timeline… but when I asked for the CRM verification — payment receipts, dues status, through the builder's own desk — suddenly it's 'why all this formality, boss, token first.' I said the formality IS the deal. He's gone quiet since yesterday.

Then he's answered you. A clean assignor treats the CRM check like a compliment — the last one sent you a Drive folder before you asked, remember. Resistance to verification is verification. Moving on — the east-facing one in tower nine: the Singapore-based assignor, premium at forty-eight lakhs over his booking. Against the builder's current release price that's six percent under, with the 2023 agreement's escalation cap travelling to you — worth another six lakhs you're not paying for. I've already emailed the transfer desk for his file. If it's clean by Friday, we move — properly, every rupee on paper.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “Gautham taught me that the assignment market is the primary market's side door — the builder's flat, the builder's process, an investor's exit, and a buyer doing his homework arriving almost-first. The mechanics are learnable: transfer fees, NOC steps, loan re-origination — and the diligence is double-layered: the project's visible construction and the assignor's verified history. His rule is absolute and expensive: every rupee on paper, every step through the builder's desk. The token-first deal at 9% below market was an unsecured loan to a stranger, declined; the assignor who resisted the CRM check answered the question by resisting it. And the prize was a 2023 agreement inherited whole — a lower escalation cap worth ₹6L of found value, premium benchmarked six percent under the builder's current releases. The best due diligence was social: three weeks in the buyers' group before committing, which taught him the amenity fight was real but resolving and the delay was four months, not the rumored twelve. The almost-first buyer inherits a position; the diplomacy of arriving second into a formed community is the part no spreadsheet covers.”

That's the side door done properly, Gautham — the grey market brought into clean legal light, every rupee on paper. You inherited a position and did the diplomacy to inherit a community. Tower nine east is yours, almost-first and fully earned.

Verify the assignor with one CRM email — receipts, dues, dispute flags — and treat resistance to verification as the answer it is. Benchmark the premium against the builder's current releases, not the scarcity story, and discount for the agreement's remaining obligations. Lawyer the inherited agreement clause by clause — 2023 terms like lower escalation caps travel with the assignment and are found value. Read the buyers' group for weeks before committing; the assignment's best due diligence is social. And hold the no-cash rule absolutely: it costs deal flow and buys clean title and sleep. The almost-first buyer inherits a position; the diplomacy of arriving second into a formed community is the part no spreadsheet covers.
